connectorUiConfig.title: Salesforce Real-Time Event Monitoring (via Codeless Connector Framework)
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown:
The Salesforce Real-Time Event Monitoring data connector provides the capability to ingest security and anomaly detection events from Salesforce into Microsoft Sentinel in near real-time. This connector accesses the [Real-Time Event Monitoring](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=xcloud.real_time_event_monitoring_events.htm&type=5) events via the Query API, enabling immediate visibility into security-related activities, credential stuffing, session hijacking, and anomalous user behavior.

**Key Capabilities:**
- **Real-time security monitoring:** Ingest events as they occur with minimal latency
- **Security-focused events:** Includes ApiAnomalyEventStore, CredentialStuffingEventStore, SessionHijackingEventStore, ReportAnomalyEventStore
- **Enhanced threat detection:** Identify suspicious activities immediately for faster incident response
- **Compliance and auditing:** Meet real-time security monitoring requirements

instructionSteps.title: Prerequisites
instructionSteps.description:
Before setting up this connector:

1. You need **Salesforce Shield** or **Event Monitoring Add-on** license
2. **System Administrator** role with **View Real-Time Event Monitoring Data** permission
3. Real-Time Event Monitoring must be **enabled** in your Salesforce org
4. **API access** through a Connected App with OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Flow

instructionSteps.title: Step 1: Verify Real-Time Event Monitoring Access
instructionSteps.description:
1. Log in to Salesforce as System Administrator
2. Navigate to **Setup** → Quick Find → **Event Manager**
3. Verify you can see Real-Time Event Types:
   - ApiAnomalyEventStore
   - CredentialStuffingEventStore
   - SessionHijackingEventStore
   - ReportAnomalyEventStore
   - PermissionSetEventStore
4. If these are not visible, contact Salesforce support to enable Real-Time Event Monitoring

instructionSteps.title: Step 2: Create Connected App for API Access
instructionSteps.description:
Follow these steps to create a Connected App:

1. Navigate to **Setup** → Quick Find → **App Manager**
2. Click **New Connected App**
3. Configure Basic Information:
   - **Connected App Name:** Microsoft Sentinel Real-Time Events
   - **API Name:** (auto-generated)
   - **Contact Email:** Your admin email
4. Enable OAuth Settings:
   - Check **Enable OAuth Settings**
   - **Callback URL:** https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/callback
   - **Enable Client Credentials Flow:** Check this box
   - **Selected OAuth Scopes:** Add "Manage user data via APIs (api)"
5. Click **Save** and then **Continue**
6. On the Connected App details page:
   - Click **Manage Consumer Details**
   - Verify your identity
   - Save the **Consumer Key** and **Consumer Secret**

instructionSteps.title: Step 3: Configure Connected App Policies
instructionSteps.description:
1. From the Connected App detail page, click **Manage**
2. Click **Edit Policies**
3. Under OAuth Policies:
   - **Client Credentials Flow:** Select a pre-authorized run-as user (must have API access)
   - **IP Relaxation:** Relax IP restrictions (or configure Azure IP ranges)
4. Click **Save**

instructionSteps.title: Step 4: Get Your Salesforce Domain Name
instructionSteps.description:
1. Navigate to **Setup** → Quick Find → **My Domain**
2. Copy your domain URL (e.g., **https://your-domain.my.salesforce.com**)
3. **Important:** Do not include a trailing slash

instructionSteps.title: Step 5: Connect to Microsoft Sentinel
instructionSteps.description: Provide your Salesforce credentials and configuration below to start ingesting Real-Time Event Monitoring data.

validations.regexMessage: Please enter a valid Salesforce domain (e.g., https://your-domain.my.salesforce.com)

instructionSteps.title: Validation
instructionSteps.description:
After connecting, validate data ingestion:

1. Wait 10-15 minutes for initial data collection
2. In Microsoft Sentinel, run this query:
   ```
   SalesforceRealTimeEvents_CL
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
   | summarize Count = count() by EventType
   ```
3. Verify you see events appearing in the table
4. If no data appears, check:
   - Real-Time Event Monitoring is enabled in Salesforce
   - Connected App has correct OAuth scopes
   - Run-as user has proper permissions
   - Domain name is correct without trailing slash
